title: Subscripts and Custom Collection Interfaces
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of subscripts and custom collection interfaces in a Swift program or workflow.
Apply declaring subscripts in a small, inspectable example.
Check the expected result and identify one boundary case or platform constraint.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on subscripts and custom collection interfaces and the practical choices around it. Start with the smallest example, connect it to “Declaring subscripts”, and verify the result before adding complexity.
content.why_it_matters: Advanced capabilities matter most when tied to actual requirements, measured behavior and clear trust boundaries—not used just because they exist.

content_blocks.text: **Start with the rule.** For declaring subscripts, separate app behavior from presentation and platform services. Define ownership and error states, test the behavior independently where possible, and verify Apple-platform requirements on a supported target.

**Work through the lesson.** Study advanced language facilities after the foundational type, generics, and concurrency models are clear. The detailed subtopic list in this lesson preserves the curriculum coverage; treat each item as a cue for a small example or a focused question rather than trying to memorize syntax.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every Swift snippet can run in a browser or on every operating system.

common_mistakes.fix: Run command-line examples locally; use Xcode or a compatible package/target for framework-specific material.
